risk_if_not_implemented: Without Kiosks & Point of Interaction (PoI) Devices, mobile and portable devices may expose organizational data through loss, theft, insecure configuration or unauthorized use. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Modification / Loss of System Integrity (R-AM-2), System / Data Compromise (Non-Technical Vector) (R-BC-5), Loss of Confidentiality (R-IP-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Physical Crime (MT-5), Fraud, Corruption and/or Intentional Criminal Conduct (MT-14), Counterfeit / Non-Conforming Products (MT-20).

compensating_control_1.name: Physical Access Control
compensating_control_1.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to enforce physical access authorizations for all physical access points (including designated entry/exit points) to facilities (excluding those areas within the facility officially designated as publicly accessible).
compensating_control_1.justification: Physical Access Control (PES-08) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Kiosks & Point of Interaction (PoI) Devices (AST-21) by restricting system and data access to authorized users through alternative identity and access mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Least Functionality
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to configure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to provide only essential capabilities by specifically prohibiting or restricting the use of ports, protocols, and/or services.
compensating_control_2.justification: Least Functionality (CFG-03) provides configuration hardening that compensates for the absence of Kiosks & Point of Interaction (PoI) Devices (AST-21) by eliminating unnecessary services and enforcing secure settings to reduce inherent exposure. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
